0328e9e1d2e36668.text: Have a drink at the bar while you're there. Nell hears even more gossip than I do, and that's saying something.

0b8e5bcdb8b2fbd7.text: Sit down if you like. Rook won't mind, and if he does, even better.

0ca4457b7921d910.text: And don't ask me why we went so far in that time. Not yet. Some stories need a full table.

23934cb1babd93ea.text: If you want news from the rest of the colony, dock at Waypost Ostra. Tamsin can take you there any time.

296a39b720ffa7ce.text: Hungry? Sit down anywhere. It's not fancy, but it's warm, and nobody out there is going to cook for you.

2aeed7d3a682d07e.text: Go on, I've got a pot on, but I'm listening.

318a44f5af81cf16.text: Brannik runs the armory and the ammo. Dace improves your weapons in the weapons room, and Wren looks after your suit in the room next door.

3cabcf8b80aa953d.text: Hey, you. I've heard a thing or two about your crew.

49e66e141d81aa0b.text: All right, I'll cook for you. But not without my galley crate. It's in Rook's old cache on Rimeback, on Lisk. We left supplies there on our way further in, a year ago, and on the way back nobody wanted to stop.

561f91ace7bdc001.text: Hungry? Come by the mess hall and sit down anywhere. It's not fancy, but it's warm, and nobody out there is going to cook for you.

67e9b2cc8d023ed6.text: I cooked in the settlements' canteen, and then for two years for Rook's crew. Good pay, long hours, and a captain who never knows when to turn back.

6bee24548015e11c.text: I left after he flew us into the storms once too often. He still keeps my seat at his table. I think he hopes I'll come back.

74cb0dfe6a0de341.text: Find the rest of your crew first. A crew that keeps coming back is worth cooking for.

7cdd4223838eb44d.text: Tamsin flies the ship. You'll find her on the bridge, or in the cockpit while we're flying. And you'll always find me in the mess hall.

803ecea533ff334c.text: I signed on to cook, but mostly I listen. Over a hot meal, people say more than they'd ever admit.

8f7b083afbf294fd.text: So you found them all: a gunsmith, a suit tech, and old Hollis, of all people. The whole bar is talking about it.

9d3e61f2cf8f5561.text: Hey, you. What's on your mind?

a6b3ba6c8114eefa.text: Now go on. I'll say goodbye to Rook and meet you at the ship.

a79c755c52dbdf13.text: Moons around a gas giant! When I signed on, I never thought I'd see Gaulm out of a window. Somebody has to tell me what it looks like from down there.

a82d26206e3c470e.text: Cook for your crew? Maybe. But I hear your ship still has empty rooms, and I've cooked for half a table long enough.

b5e158ef98c6529a.text: My crate! Still sealed, and it still smells of Rook's terrible coffee.

bfe4447353106799.text: Most of what I hear is nonsense. Some of it isn't. The trick is telling the difference.

d0b30538669e3f60.text: Hollis keeps the miners going. Ilse has the medical bay at the nose, and Okoro is down in the engine room with the heat shield.

d65f91969975af43.text: Everyone comes through my mess hall sooner or later. So if you want to know what's going on aboard, I'm the one to ask.

eb7b1cc9c67fd0ec.text: What can I tell you? I know everybody's business here.

fa2fee468331efff.text: Rook won't go back for it, and I won't ask him. Bring it to me, and I'll start packing.
